title: Double While Found
statement:
You get an integer array nums and a starting value start. Repeat this: if start appears anywhere in nums, double it. Stop as soon as the current value is not in nums.

Return the final value.

examples.why: 3, 6, 12 and 24 are all present, in any order. 48 is not, so it stops there.
4 is missing, so the chain breaks even though 8 and 16 are present.
start is not in the array, so it never changes.

hints: The order of nums does not matter, only which values are present.
You may test membership many times. What makes each test O(1)?
Put nums in a set. Then loop: while the set contains start, double start.

explain.intuition:
The process only ever asks one question: is this value in the array? Scanning the whole array for each question costs O(n) each time. Since the value doubles every round and values are bounded, there are only about log(1000) ≈ 10 rounds, but a hash set still makes each question O(1) and the intent obvious.

Sorting gives another clean pass: in sorted order the values you need appear in increasing order, so walk once and double start whenever the current element equals it.
steps: While the set contains start, set start = start × 2.
pitfalls: Walking the unsorted array once from left to right and doubling on a match. In the first example 24 comes before 12, so a single unsorted pass stops too early.
Stopping after the first doubling instead of repeating.
Removing values from the set as you go and then mishandling duplicates. Not needed: each value is checked at most once anyway.

solutions.title: Sort, then one pass
solutions.idea: In sorted order the chain's values appear in increasing order, so a single walk can double start each time it meets it.

solutions.title: Hash set
solutions.idea: Store the values, then keep doubling while the current value is stored.

followups: Answer many different start values on the same array. How do you avoid rebuilding anything?
Since values are at most 1000, can a bitmask of the powers-of-two multiples answer each query in O(1)?
lcTitle: Keep Multiplying Found Values by Two
